Which of the following integrals gives the arc length of the polar curve $r=1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )$ for $-\,\frac{\pi }{4}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}$ (shown in blue in the  diagram above)?
worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ),$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ).
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ))^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+{sin}^{2}⁡(2\theta )+4{cos}^{2}⁡(2\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+1+3{cos}^{2}⁡(2\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{2+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+3{cos}^{2}⁡(2\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
